Tabular overview of a document's top-level blocks

Source: R/ast-summary.R
ast_summary.Rd

Usage

ast_summary(x, max_text = 40L)

Arguments

x

A pandoc document, a pandoc_blocks wrapper, or a plain list of top-level blocks.

max_text

Maximum width of the truncated text preview.

Value

A data.frame with columns type (S7 class name), level (header level or NA), id (@attr@id or NA), section (deepest enclosing heading title, from ast_sections()), text (truncated ast_text() preview), and node (a list-column of the block objects). The node column displays as compact <type> placeholders but holds the live S7 objects for piping back through the verbs.

Details

Returns a one-row-per-top-level-block data.frame summarising a pandoc document, the analog of parsermd's as_tibble.rmd_ast(). It makes a document graspable at a glance and bridges to base/dplyr filtering: the node list-column holds the live S7 objects, so a filtered frame can be fed straight back through the selection and mutation verbs.

The view is deliberately shallow (top-level blocks only) to mirror parsermd's flat model; reach for select_descendants() to inspect nested content.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
doc = parse_qmd("# A\n\nsome text\n\n## B\n\nmore\n")
ast_summary(doc)
} # }
